jobs.description: Pomona College, Department of Biology Position ID:Pomona-Department of Biology-AP [#32243] Position Title: Assistant Professor of Biology Position Type:Tenured/Tenure-track faculty Position Location:Claremont, California 91711, United States of America [map] Subject Area: Cell Biology / Cellular Biology Appl Deadline:2026/10/02 03:59 AM UTC (posted 2026/09/03 04:00 AM UTC, updated 2026/06/24, listed until 2026/10/02 03:59 AM UTC) Position Description: Apply Position Description The Department of Biology is hiring a tenure track assistant professor of biology to join the department in July 2027. We are seeking a plant biologist in any area of plant biology, however those with an interest in plant physiology are especially encouraged to apply. We are looking for candidates with a demonstrated interest in teaching and conducting research with undergraduate students. The successful candidate will offer an upper-level course in Plant Physiology or other upper-level plant biology course with laboratory, and teach an introductory course with laboratory. Pomona College is a private, undergraduate, selective liberal arts institution enrolling approximately 1,700 students. Pomona College is the oldest and founding member of the Claremont Colleges, a consortium of institutions that include five undergraduate colleges and two graduate universities, located in southern California. Intercollegiate collaboration among the colleges provides university-scale services and facilities, including the Bernard Field Station and the Claremont Colleges Libraries. While each institution is independent, undergraduate students can take courses at any of the colleges and research collaboration among faculty is encouraged through professional development networks. Pomona faculty in the Environmental Analysis Department partner regularly with colleagues in and beyond Claremont. The faculty in Biology welcome applicants who are committed to high quality, innovative undergraduate teaching and to mentoring undergraduate student research. Pomona College’s plant growth facility includes greenhouses, growth chambers, and a headhouse for planting, preparation, and storage, with a full-time dedicated greenhouse manager (more detailed information on the facilities is available). The College actively promotes a dynamic and inclusive environment in which students and employees of diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives can learn and work. Pomona College is an equal opportunity employer that welcomes members of all groups and reaffirms its commitment not to discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, gender, age, religion, caste, gender identity or expression, disability, or sexual orientation in its educational programs, activities, and employment practices. In recent years, over 51% of entering classes identified as students of color, 23% as first-generation, 14% international, and nearly 20% as Pell eligible students. Recruiting and retaining a diverse faculty committed to building an inclusive community is vital to educating an equally diverse student body. Candidates who can contribute to this goal are particularly encouraged to apply. Preferred Qualifications: A Ph.D. in a field of biology by the start of employment and expertise in plant biology is required. Teaching experience; a demonstrated commitment to undergraduate teaching and research; and a commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, in biology are also priorities. Minimum Qualifications: Ph.D. in a field of biology by the start of employment and expertise in plant biology. jobs.description: Pomona College, Computer Science Position ID:Pomona-Computer Science-ASSTPROF [#32241] Position Title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science Position Type:Tenured/Tenure-track faculty Position Location:Claremont, California 91711, United States of America [map] Subject Area: Computer Science / All areas Appl Deadline:2026/10/05 03:59 AM UTC (accepting applications posted 2026/07/01 04:00 AM UTC, updated 2026/06/24, listed until 2026/10/13 03:59 AM UTC) Position Description: Apply Position Description Pomona College seeks applications for an Assistant Professor of Computer Science to begin on July 1, 2027. We seek candidates with a strong commitment to i) inclusive undergraduate teaching across all levels of our curriculum; ii) mentoring a diverse student body and fostering a supportive learning environment; iii) developing a strong, independent research program that involves undergraduates and leads to peer-reviewed publications; and iv) helping build community within our Department and the College.We welcome applicants with broad intellectual interests from a wide range of subdisciplines, with a preference for candidates whose research and teaching interests complement those of the current faculty (Computer Science Department Website) or who can contribute to expanding the department's curricular range and scholarly interests. The teaching commitment is four courses per year over two semesters of instruction (2-2). CS faculty are expected to teach at least two required courses among our introductory (introduction to programming and computer science, mathematical foundations, and data structures) and/or core (algorithms, languages and theory of computation, and computer systems) sequences. Candidates should have a Ph.D. in hand by their start date, usually July 1, 2027.Our department values experience working with undergraduate students from diverse backgrounds and a commitment to improving higher education for underrepresented students through teaching, scholarship, or service. After graduation, recent CS majors have taken jobs in industry and national research labs, and have pursued graduate programs at top research labs.Pomona College, located in Southern California, is the founding member of the Claremont Colleges, which also includes Claremont McKenna, Scripps, Pitzer, Harvey Mudd, and Claremont Graduate University. Students can cross-register for courses at any of the colleges, which allows Pomona students to enjoy the advantages of personalized instruction and close faculty-student interaction combined with the intellectual and extracurricular resources typically found at much larger universities. Pomona's Computer Science department currently has 10 full-time, tenured or tenure-track faculty members, and there are over 30 CS faculty across the Claremont Colleges. In collaboration with the Claremont College Consortium, Pomona College offers a variety of professional development, mentorship, and networking opportunities for junior faculty, including the opportunity for entering faculty members to apply for a fully funded leave in their fourth year at the College.A complete application includes a cover letter, a detailed curriculum vitae, graduate transcripts, three brief statements–one addressing the candidate’s teaching philosophy, one addressing the candidate’s scholarship, and one addressing the candidate’s ability to mentor a diverse student body and three or more letters of reference, at least one of which evaluates the candidate's teaching. Please upload electronic copies of all materials to Academic Jobs Online #32241.Review of applications will begin on October 4, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. The salary for this position will range from $105,000 to $135,000 and will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to internal equity, experience, education, specialty, and training. jobs.title: Assistant Professor of English
jobs.description: Pomona College, English Position ID:Pomona-English-AP [#32246] Position Title: Assistant Professor of English Position Type:Tenured/Tenure-track faculty Position Location:Claremont, California 91711, United States of America [map] Subject Area: Latinx Appl Deadline: (posted 2026/07/01 04:00 AM UTC, updated 2026/06/24, listed until 2026/12/25 04:59 AM UTC) Position Description: Apply Position Description The English Department at Pomona College invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor to begin Fall 2027. At a moment when the department is in conversation about diversifying the major as well as building on its current strengths, we seek a colleague whose research focuses on US-Latinx literature and culture. We are open to various areas of expertise. Transnational, hemispheric, and/or comparative approaches welcome. Areas of interest may include but are not limited to: decolonial solidarity frameworks, environmental and digital humanities, migration, border and critical refugee studies, gender and sexuality, performance, aesthetics, global South, and considerations of the more-than-human. We seek to attract, develop, and retain faculty that contribute to the cultural, linguistic, experiential, and diverse curricular offerings of the department. The teaching load at Pomona College is two courses per semester. Faculty are expected to teach across all levels of the undergraduate curriculum and are eligible for generous teaching and research grants. Candidates should have Ph.D. in hand at time of appointment. Complete application includes: (a) cover letter, (b) curriculum vitae, (c) graduate transcripts, (d) three brief, 1-page statements – one addressing teaching philosophy and experience, one addressing scholarship and future research directions, and one addressing demonstrated ability to mentor a diverse student body (e) three letters of recommendations (f) writing sample 20pp. Please apply through Academic Jobs Online #32246. Review of applications begins October 15, 2026. Pomona College is a highly selective private liberal arts college with an enrollment of approximately 1750 students, all undergraduates, and a student-faculty ratio of eight to one. The College and the Department support equal access to higher education and value working in a richly diverse environment. Of the students admitted into the Class of 2024, 58.8% self-identify as domestic students of color, 13.6% international and 20.7% are first generation college students. The successful candidate will have the ability to teach and mentor exceptional students of diverse backgrounds–utilizing pedagogical practices that are rigorous, inclusive, and which promote academic equity. Pomona is the founding member of The Claremont Colleges, a unique constellation of five small undergraduate colleges and two graduate institutions located in beautiful Southern California near the foothills of the San Gabriel mountains, about 35 miles east of Los Angeles. Students of the Claremont Colleges can cross-register for courses at any of the colleges and have access to a shared library system containing over 2 million volumes. Pomona students thus enjoy the advantages of personalized instruction and close faculty-student interaction in a small liberal arts college setting, combined with the intellectual and extracurricular resources typically found at much larger universities. Pomona College offers robust compensation. The salary for this position will range from $105,000 to $125,000 and will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to internal equity, experience, education, specialty, and training. For any questions, please contact Dr. Cherene Sherrard-Johnson, Search Committee Chair and Department Chair, cherene.sherrard-johnson@pomona.edu. jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Environmental Analysis (Critical Geographer)
jobs.description: Pomona College, Environmental Analysis Position ID:Pomona-EA-AP [#32245] Position Title: Assistant Professor of Environmental Analysis Position Type:Tenured/Tenure-track faculty Position Location:Claremont, California 91711, United States of America [map] Subject Area: Environmental Analysis / Critical Geography Appl Deadline:2026/11/01 03:59 AM UTC (posted 2026/07/01 04:00 AM UTC, updated 2026/06/24, listed until 2026/12/25 04:59 AM UTC) Position Description: Apply Position Description Pomona College invites applications for a tenure‑track Assistant Professor of Environmental Analysis specializing in critical geography, broadly conceived, beginning July 1, 2027. We seek a scholar‑teacher committed to excellent undergraduate education whose research and teaching examine relationships among space, environment, power, and social inequality, including social‑scientific approaches to sustainability in urban and built environments. The successful candidate will: • Teach EA010 (Introduction to Environmental Analysis) and contribute to the core curriculum through critical perspectives on space, environment, and society. • Teach additional undergraduate courses at the intermediate and advanced levels in critical geography and related areas, which may include human–environment relations, political ecology, or social dimensions of urban and regional geographies. • Teach and develop courses that integrate geospatial technologies and spatial analysis, such as ArcGIS, QGIS, and related tools, with attention to social, political, and environmental contexts. • Maintain an active, peer‑reviewed program of scholarship. • Mentor undergraduate research and supervise senior thesis projects. • Contribute, as appropriate, to interdisciplinary programs across Pomona College and the Claremont Colleges. Qualifications • Ph.D. in Geography or a related field by the time of appointment. Applicants who are ABD and expect to complete all degree requirements by Dec. 2027 are encouraged to apply. • Expertise in GIS and spatial methodologies, with the ability to teach these tools in ways that foreground social, environmental, and ethical considerations. • Evidence of scholarly contributions consistent with tenure expectations. • Demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in teaching, scholarship, and mentoring. Please submit your application online at Academic Jobs Online #32245 and include: (a) cover letter, (b) curriculum vitae, (c) three 1-2 page statements – one describing teaching philosophy and experience, one describing research including future directions, and one describing a demonstrated ability to mentor a diverse student body (see Preparing your Equity and Inclusion Statement), and (d) summary of teaching evaluations. You must also provide three letters of recommendation: the application site will prompt you to enter your recommenders’ contact information. Candidates who proceed to the next round will be asked for a sample of scholarly work such as an article-length paper or its equivalent. Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and will continue until the position is filled. Pomona College offers a robust compensation package. The salary range for this position is $95,000 - $115,000. Pomona College, the founding member of the Claremont Colleges, is a highly selective liberal arts college attracting a diverse community of approximately 1700 students. It is part of the Claremont Consortium, which includes the five Claremont Colleges, the Claremont Graduate University, and the Keck Graduate Institute. For further information, please contact Marc Los Huertos, marc.loshuertos@pomona.edu, chair of the search committee. jobs.description: Pomona College, Psychology Position ID:Pomona-Psychology-AP [#32248] Position Title: Assistant Professor of Psychological Science & Neuroscience Position Type:Tenured/Tenure-track faculty Position Location:Claremont, California 91711, United States of America Subject Areas: Psychology / Behavioral NeuroscienceNeuroscience / Behavioral Appl Deadline:2026/10/16 03:59 AM UTC (posted 2026/07/01 04:00 AM UTC, updated 2026/06/24, listed until 2026/12/25 04:59 AM UTC) Position Description: Position Description Pomona College Tenure-Track Assistant Professor in Psychological Science and Neuroscience. The Departments of Psychological Science and Neuroscience seek candidates with a demonstrated commitment to teaching and the ability to establish an active research program that involves undergraduates. The position (75% appointment in Psychological Science and 25% appointment in Neuroscience) will begin in July 2027. The candidate is expected to teach two courses per semester, in addition to supervising senior theses. Courses may include introductory psychology and/or human neuroscience, as well as courses (elective, lab, or seminar) in the candidate’s area of research expertise. The successful candidate will have a productive research program examining the neural and/or physiological mechanisms of psychological phenomena. Pomona College is a selective liberal arts college, known for small classes, a challenging curriculum, and close relationships between students and faculty. The College has a generous pre-tenure sabbatical and offers internal support for faculty research, as well as professional development opportunities for faculty at all stages of their careers. The Departments of Psychological Science and Neuroscience are strongly committed to inclusive excellence in teaching and mentoring a diverse student body. Candidates should have a Ph.D. in Psychology, Neuroscience, or a related field. Please submit a dossier including (a) a cover letter, (b) curriculum vitae, (c) three brief statements – one addressing teaching philosophy and experience; one addressing scholarship, including future directions; and one addressing the candidate’s ability to mentor a diverse student body, (d) up to three representative reprints or pre-prints, and (e) three letters of recommendation. Similarly, faculty of all contract types are eligible for this funding. Awards will be made in these two categories. The base amount of each award is $6,000: $5,000 for a student research stipend plus fringe benefits; $1,000 stipend for supplies or travel related to the research project. Note that the student stipend amount is subject to change, and awards will be adjusted accordingly. Faculty Research, Scholarship, or Creative Work Awards (without a student). In support of faculty projects that advance professional and scholarly development. Base amount: $3,500 for supplies, travel, supplemental salary or other expenses. In both Categories 1 and 2, there is additional funding this year from the Hixon-Riggs Forum for Responsive Science and Engineering, supporting faculty and student research that examines the social dimensions of science and/or technology. In particular, this funding is intended to support projects in which questions about the relationships between science, technology, and society are central to the investigation. Interdisciplinary projects drawing on research methods from STEM and HSA fields are especially encouraged. All internal awards should be spent between Jan. 1, 2022 and Dec. 31, 2022. Student faculty research award stipends should be used during the summer months. Additional Funding: Proposers may request up to $1,000 in additional funding with justification. The RPI Committee will accept rolling applications throughout the spring as long as funding is available. Full proposals for either time track should be submitted electronically to the following Google Form links: Summer 2022 Student-Faculty Research Mentorship Awards Summer 2022 Faculty Research, Scholarship, and Creative Works Awards Proposals should be understandable by any member of the Harvey Mudd College faculty. jobs.description: Job Posting Location: Claremont, CA Job Posting Title: Lecturer in Psychological Science Job Description: ABOUT POMONA COLLEGE: Located near Los Angeles, California, Pomona College is widely regarded as one of the nation's premier liberal arts colleges. Established in 1887, Pomona College is known for small classes, a challenging curriculum, close relationships between students and faculty, and a range of student research and leadership opportunities. Pomona is a member of The Claremont Colleges. The Psychological Science Department at Pomona College invites applications for two temporary, part-time Lecturers for Spring 2027/academic year, 2026-2027. The specific discipline is open, although candidates able to teach electives in sports psychology, clinical neuropsychology, development, or developmental psychopathology are preferred. Each position has a teaching load of one course to be taught in the Spring Semester. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS : The successful candidate will have demonstrated ability or potential to teach and mentor exceptional students of diverse backgrounds—utilizing pedagogical practices that are rigorous, inclusive, and which promote academic equity. QUALIFICATIONS: Education--Required: Ph.D. in hand by July 1, 2026 ABD welcome to apply. Teaching Experience--Preferred: Demonstrable experience teaching in the candidate’s area of expertise is preferred. TO APPLY: Upload a single PDF document (up to 5MB) to Pomona College’s online portal, that includes: Cover Letter including information about elective courses the candidate can offer, CV, and a Teaching Statement that speaks to teaching in a liberal arts context. Teach Evaluations are optional. Review of completed applications will begin on September 21st and will continue until the position is filled. Please note: Employment is contingent upon providing proof of the legal right to work in the United States as required by the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986 for the duration of the contract, January 1, 2027 – May 31, 2027. Compensation for this position ranges between $9,000 – $9,900 per course. Salary is commensurate with years in rank and teaching experience. Compensation will be paid in equal monthly installments between January and May, depending on the contract. As an equal opportunity workplace, Pomona College is committed to fairness regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, ability, gender identity or Veteran status. Through its Strategic Vision, Pomona College remains steadfast in its goal of creating workplace environments where all can flourish. The department welcomes applications from scholars who are ready to contribute to providing equitable access to education and expanding opportunities in the liberal arts and natural sciences. REQUIREMENTS: For the Spring Semester, the contract period is January 1, 2027 through May 31, 2027, with instruction beginning on Tuesday, January 19, 2027. After submitting proof of work authorization and completing onboarding, lecturers are expected to prepare for their classes. This non-tenure-track position is instructional and does not require student advising, faculty service or participation in faculty governance.
